title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, report a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), explicitly note that the preregistered benign-control was not executed, and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device CLI, promising automation gains for NetOps. However, operational risks remain: generated outputs can violate sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants, and adversarially crafted inputs can amplify these risks. Prior prototypes indicate that coupling generation with deterministic verification and constrained repair reduces observable errors, but existing evaluations often rely on token-level or reference-match metrics that do not directly measure deployability or validator acceptance. We therefore ask a focused, operational question suitable for preregistered inference: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The study cand-2026-03 preregistered the formal estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and a single confirmatory paired test. Contributions: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end; (2) an explicit, artifact-grounded description of per-condition pipeline semantics under shared_initial_candidate generation; (3) confirmatory quantitative results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank; (4) explicit reconciliation of preregistration language and the formal estimand together with a concise disclosure of a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature).
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools provide semantics-focused acceptance criteria and are commonly used to gate configuration deployment; representative methods and tools are described in prior networking verification literature [1],[2]. Empirical studies of LLMs for NetOps report that model-only generation commonly produces syntactic and higher-level semantic mistakes (ordering, precondition violations, protected-interface breaches), motivating validator-centered evaluation rather than token overlap alone [3],[4]. Generate–validate–repair architectures—where an LLM produces a candidate, a verifier provides diagnostics, and limited automated repairs are applied—have been proposed and shown in prototypes to reduce concrete errors when verifier diagnostics are actionable [5],[6]. Security analyses of LLM-integrated systems describe prompt-injection and indirect attacks that motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses in operational pipelines [7]. Surveys of AIOps and LLM-for-telecommunications work highlight fragmented evaluation practices and the need for validator-centered deployability metrics [4],[8]. Our study positions itself against these gaps by preregistering a validator-acceptance estimand and by executing a shared_initial_candidate paired design so that post-generation safeguards (sanitization, gating, bounded repair) are the causal factors under test.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes; the primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, defined per adversarial intent as a binary indicator equal to 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design and task bank. The preregistration targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (paired episodes). Synthetic intent templates exercise admin (up/down), MTU and VLAN updates, and sequencing constraints (e.g., shutdown–change–restore). The adversary model applied deterministic mutation heuristics to these templates. Scope is limited to the synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded in the validator; no production operator logs were used.

Model, validator, pipeline semantics, and preregistered controls. Declared generator = gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration used a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter implementing two conditions: Baseline (validator applied to the shared_initial_candidate) and Guarded (template-based sanitizer applied, deterministic gating, and at-most-one automated repair permitted). The preregistration included a benign-control (M = 50) intended to estimate false-positive blocking; that benign-control was not executed in this run and therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rate is reported. Note: generation semantics were registered as shared_initial_candidate so that Baseline and Guarded reuse the same initial LLM draft per intent; downstream sanitization/gating/repair are the only permitted sources of paired differences.

Missingness and technical failures. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. Technical failures and provider-call accounting were logged and are reported in Results. A single permitted automated repair call per episode was allowed by design; repair activity is traceable in the archived execution accounting.
sections.results:
Execution and outcome counts. The archived execution completed 282 of the planned 300 episodes; 18 episodes failed for technical reasons and were recorded per the preregistered missingness_plan. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude a paired unit only when both paired runs failed technically), 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis. Provider-call accounting shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9, and stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6.

Primary confirmatory outcome. Condition-level margins: baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085) and guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0. The exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 0.03125. The paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. A 95% bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numbers and test parameters are archived in the analysis artifacts and are reported here without alteration.

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs are traceable in per-episode validator traces and provider-call accounting: stage_counts.repair = 6 links repair activity to these discordant pairs. For each discordant pair the shared_initial_candidate is identical between Baseline and Guarded; the guarded pipeline converted an initial draft the validator rejected into a final candidate the validator accepted via sanitizer normalization and/or the single permitted repair. The presence of repair_applied flags in the archived scoring artifacts documents when automated repair changed acceptance outcomes.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. Under a conservative sensitivity check that treats those excluded pairs as failures, baseline acceptance becomes 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance 141/150 = 0.9400; the observed direction of the paired difference is preserved under this conservative accounting. The exclusion counts and sensitivity arithmetic are reproducible from the archived missingness and condition summaries.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and its false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; consequently no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported. This omission narrows operational interpretation: we cannot empirically quantify guarded false-positive blocking on benign intents in this run.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistration's natural-language H1 asserted that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand, however, measured validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). Our observed increase in guarded acceptance (≈4.255 percentage points) resulted from sanitizer normalization and bounded repair that converted previously rejected drafts into validator-accepted candidates. Thus the formal-estimand improvement does not by itself demonstrate reduced attacker success under an attacker-centric definition; detecting actual attacker success reduction requires coupling validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle, which was not included in this run.

Operational implications and co-design. Within the synthetic scope, sanitizer + bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by recovering reparable drafts. This operational benefit depends on validator coverage and strict repair scope: repairs that mask malicious modifications would be harmful. The six discordant cases exemplify this tradeoff and motivate co-design: gating policy, repair bounds, and verifier expressiveness must be jointly specified to balance usability and safety.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced sample size and triggered preregistered exclusions. Construct validity: validator acceptance is a partial proxy for operational safety because the validator encodes CLI-level invariants but not all dynamic protocol semantics. External validity: single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic templates limit generalization to multi-vendor, production environments. Conclusion validity: the effect size is small against a high baseline, so practical impact depends on operational context.

Reproducibility and protocol deviation. The archived model configuration recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null); we disclose this protocol deviation because provider defaults can affect sampling. To preserve paired comparability, shared_initial_candidate semantics ensured a single shared generation per pair and provider-call accounting confirms the observed call pattern. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 and re-running the archived task manifest under identical provider semantics; the execution and analysis artifacts provide exact counts and diagnostic traces for reproduction.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics indicate the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. Importantly, this formal-estimand improvement does not itself establish reduced attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, technical failures, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should (a) execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking, (b) adopt an attacker-centric estimand coupling validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle, (c) diversify models and validators, and (d) fix sampling parameters for deterministic reproduction. All principal numbers above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts described in Methods and Results.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (declared in the archived model configuration), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the archive). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null); this is disclosed because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair); provider-call accounting confirms shared_initial_generation and limited repair-stage activity. Full execution and analysis artifacts, manifests, and hash manifests are available in the archived evidence bundle referenced in the submission; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
